newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen easing on U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen easing on U.S. rate fears.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to remain little changed at the opening Thursday with a slight negative bias, dealers said.
"The market has cleared the Congress hurdle but a jump in U.S. long bond yields today, reflecting new interest rate fears, is likely to hurt sentiment," said Norman Trabucco of brokers Zaracan.

The lower house of Congress Wednesday night finally approved the government's tax reform package, which is likely to be voted into law next week by the Senate. Traders had said the five-week-old bills were long discounted by the markets.
The U.S. long bond yield rose to 7.06 percent from 7.0 percent Monday on strong housing starts, which fueled rate worries ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve.
"We're very conditioned by the mood on Wall Street ahead of the Fed debate," said Trabucco. "But there's another factor bothering the bolsa -- all this sudden talk of a devaluation."

He said the fact not only veteran liberal leader Alvaro Alsogaray but also former government economic advisor Guillermo Calvo and powerful businessman Jorge Born had suggested recently the peso currency is overvalued, was beginning to create some anxiety in the markets.
"I'm not saying it will have a major impact. But it's a negative factor which generates uncertainty and helps keep volumes low," said Trabucco.

Argentina's peso has been pegged at parity with the dollar since April 1991 under the convertibility program launched by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, who was sacked July 29 by President Carlos Menem.
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index .MERV added 0.5 percent Wednesday to 547.81 and stands 7.5 percent higher so far in September.
